newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina takes over tiny Princeville. [CORRECTED 20:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina takes over tiny Princeville. [CORRECTED 20:20 GMT]

text.p: A North Carolina state agency has taken over financial control of Princeville, a small Edgecombe County town founded by freed slaves, state officials said Thursday.

The state Local Government Commission voted unanimously Tuesday to take over the town, which has a $120,000 deficit in its annual budget of about $700,000, said Craig Barfield, director of fiscal management for the commission.

The town of 1,900 (corrects from 190,000) residents has about $96,000 of water-sewer revenue bonds outstanding. Barfield said there was no danger of default because the commission guarantees local government bonds, and has authority to intercept state sales tax distributions in order to make debt service payments.
Commission officials did intercept the state distributions in order to make the town's last debt service payment in November, Barfield said.

When the prior payment was due in June, he said, they did not formally intercept the money but "We told them we would be down there on the day the distribution was wired to their account and that we'd be there to pick up a certified check to mail it to the escrow agent," Barfield said.

The commission has been trying to help the town solve its financial woes for about 18 months. Barfield attributed the town's deficit to "management problems," including poor record keeping and failure to follow through on revenue collections.
The Charlotte Observer said Princeville did not have accurate addresses for 80 percent of its water-sewer customers, and only 51 percent of property owners paid their taxes in the last fiscal year.

Barfield said the state takeover was triggered by a threat to public health "of an urgent nature." Specifically, the town does not have enough money to repair pumps that have allowed raw sewage to leak onto its streets.

Barfield said the commission may allow a takeover of the town's water-sewer operations by neighboring Tarboro, which owns the system. Barfield has only a distribution system, and not a treatment plant.
Princeville's one-man police force has already been disbanded to cut costs.

The commission has authority to raise property taxes, and will run Princeville's finances as long as necessary "to ensure the budget's adhered to and proper internal controls are in place to record cash receipts and make disbursements," Barfield said.
He said the town's structure is uncomplicated.
"They have a general fund and a water-sewer fund. It's not a complex situation," Barfield said.
The municipal takeover was the first in North Carolina history.
"We're treading new ground here," Barfield said.

The prediminantly black communtiy was incorporated in 1885 and was one of the first in the United States to be chartered by former slaves. It previously went under the names Freedom Hill and Liberty Hill, and was created when free blacks gathered for protection around a detachment of Union troops deployed near Tarboro.
